_note: Per-station photo quest: themed text for the player, generic quest id for Gemini (data/photo-quests.json), so it can be done at any platform. Keyed by UI slug (components/run/stations.ts).

alewife.prompt: The alewife herring are lost on their way upstream! Find an arrow to point them home.

davis.prompt: Davis Square was a busy rail crossing long before the music. Find a map and trace the crossing.

porter.prompt: Travelers once rested at the old Porter House hotel. Find a seat and rest yours.

harvard.prompt: The statue in Harvard Yard tells three lies. Find a sign with writing on it. Is it telling the truth?

central.prompt: City Hall was a gift to Cambridge in 1889. Every gift needs a way in: find a door or a gate.

kendall.prompt: MIT crossed the river in 1916 and built in steel. Find something made of metal.

charles.prompt: Surgeons first used ether here in 1846, under a dome full of light. Find a light.

park.prompt: America's first subway tunnel opened here in 1897. Find the stairs that lead down into it.

downtown.prompt: Washington Street once ran along the Neck, the only road into Boston. Find something {color} like the line that runs under it now.

south.prompt: In 1899 South Station was one of the busiest on Earth. Find a number: a track, a time, anything from the timetable.

lechmere.prompt: Richard Lechmere's land was seized in the Revolution. Find a door or gate he'd have been locked out of.

science.prompt: The Museum of Science sits on top of the old Charles River Dam. Find something metal holding something up.

north.prompt: A wave of molasses swept these streets in 1919. Quick, find something {color} before it gets sticky!

haymarket.prompt: Haymarket's stalls have sold produce for nearly two centuries. Find a seat where a merchant could set up shop.

gov.prompt: Scollay Square vanished under City Hall Plaza. Find a sign with writing: a clue to what used to be here.

boylston.prompt: Boylston opened in 1897, one of the oldest subway stops in the Americas. Find a light in its old tunnels.

arlington.prompt: The Swan Boats are pedaled by foot in the Public Garden upstairs. Find the stairs or escalator up to them.

copley.prompt: Trinity Church stands on 4,500 wooden pilings just above you. Find a map of what's up there.

hynes.prompt: Mayor John B. Hynes ran Boston through the 1950s. Find a number he could have signed off on.

kenmore.prompt: The neon sign over Kenmore Square has glowed since 1965. Find something {color} that would look good in neon.

sullivan.prompt: Sullivan Square is named for Governor James Sullivan. Find a sign with a name on it.

ccollege.prompt: The Battle of Bunker Hill was fought uphill in 1775. Find stairs and take the high ground.

state.prompt: In 1776 the Declaration was read from the balcony right above you. Find a sign with writing and read it out loud!

chinatown.prompt: Chinatown's gate welcomes everyone. Find a door or a gate of your own.

backbay.prompt: Back Bay was a tidal flat until the 1800s. Find something {color} on solid ground.

ruggles.prompt: The old elevated tracks came down in 1987. Find something metal that's still standing.

foresthills.prompt: The Arnold Arboretum next door grows in the sunlight. Find a light down here instead.
